subject: geography
title: Trade Flows & Supranational Bodies
welcome_lead: Map global trade and the institutions that govern it.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on global trade flows, WTO, IMF and uneven development.
final_note: Supranational bodies shape uneven global integration.

concepts.def: Increasing interconnection of economies, cultures, politics through trade, ICT, migration.
World Trade Organization (164 members, 1995); reduces tariffs and resolves disputes.
International Monetary Fund (190 members); structural adjustment loans, often criticised for conditionality.
Provides development loans; HIPC initiative cancelled debt for 37 countries.
Group of countries with reduced internal trade barriers; EU, NAFTA/USMCA, ASEAN.
Global core-periphery patterns; high-income vs low-income GDP per capita gap.

walkthroughs.body_html: Global merchandise exports reached $24 trillion in 2022 (WTO). China leads with $3.6 trillion; USA second. South-South trade now exceeds North-South. Just-in-time supply chains link iPhone components from 43 countries.

WTO replaced GATT in 1995; Most Favoured Nation principle prevents discrimination. Doha Round stalled over agricultural subsidies. Disputes include EU vs USA over Boeing-Airbus subsidies, resolved 2021 after 17 years.

IMF Structural Adjustment Programmes required cuts to public spending, privatisation, devaluation. Critics (Stiglitz) argue these worsened poverty. HIPC initiative since 1996 cancelled $76 billion of debt for low-income countries.
